request.what: Reduce the Cardano committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal would change committeeMinSize from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize of 7.

If Constitutional Committee membership drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two members retire or their terms expire, assuming a current 7 member body.
The proposal depends temporally on another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model settings, with no technical interaction between the changed parameters.
The change does not directly alter the current number of Constitutional Committee members and does not change the maximum number of Constitutional Committee members.
With a 2/3 Constitutional Committee voting threshold, a 5-member committee would require 4 constitutional votes to meet the threshold and 2 unconstitutional votes to prevent the threshold.
At a Constitutional Committee size of 5, the inactivity of one member would allow another member to fully veto governance actions.
The proposal says the change satisfies guardrails CMS-01, CMS-02, and CMS-03 because committeeMinSize would be 5.

The proposal says the change is reversible if at least 7 Constitutional Committee members exist, but reverting to 7 while fewer than 7 members are seated would immediately halt governance until enough members were elected.

summary: The proposal requests a non-treasury parameter change lowering committeeMinSize from 7 to 5, arguing it improves governance operational resilience while acknowledging increased veto risk at lower committee size and providing a conditional reversion plan.
